A panel of US FDA advisors voted that there is reasonable evidence that GRAIL’s
multi-cancer early detection blood test Galleri is effective. The vote was 6-4.

Members of the Molecular and Clinical Genetics Panel of the Medical Devices Advisory Committee also voted 10-0 that the test is sage, and 7-2 with one abstention that the benefits of the test outweigh the risks. Those risks include false positive or negative readings.

Panel member Victor van Berkel of University of Louisville Physicians said that “if we can find more early-stage cancers in the population that we can’t screen for currently, that will end up having benefit.”
Some members noted, however, that the test should be used in addition to current cancer screening methods, rather than a replacement.
While the Galleri test is currently available in the US through cash payment, approval would mean coverage by Medicare and private insurance.

title: GRAIL's Galleri test wins endorsement from FDA panel
